and he fled to Erbil to Muzaffar al-Din.
And the Mosulites returned to their place.
Then ambassadors came from Caliph al-Nasir and from al-Malik al-Ashraf,
and they made peace between them,
and reconciled them.
And during those days when peace was established,
that boy, Nur al-Din, son of al-Malik al-Qahir, lord of Mosul, died,
because he was constantly sickly,
and scarcely once in ten days did he ride and show himself.
Then Badr al-Din took his brother, a little child of three years,
whose name was Nasir al-Din Mahmud,
and set him in his brother's place,
and made the nobles take an oath in the presence of the boy,
and mounted him on horseback and showed him to the common people.
And the heart of the people was pleased
that they saw that they had a king from the house of the Atabeg,
because they loved this house very much.
And when Nur al-Din died,
and the little boy, his brother, arose in his place,
Muzaffar al-Din and Zengi again provoked the Mosulites,
and began to plunder the country.
Because Badr al-Din had sent the majority of the forces of Mosul to Aleppo to al-Malik al-Ashraf, who wished to invade and take spoils in the territory of the Franks,
he sent to Aybak, the commander of al-Ashraf's army, who had been sent to Nisibis,
and brought him to him.
And when Badr al-Din saw how few in number were those who had come with Aybak, the slave of al-Ashraf,
he was disheartened and also discouraged,
because those whom he had sent to al-Ashraf were many more than those who had been sent to him by al-Ashraf.
However, that Aybak began to act haughtily
and urged
Badr al-Din that they should cross the Tigris and go plunder the territory of Erbil.
Now Muzaffar al-Din, when he heard this,
gathered his forces and crossed the Zab.
And Badr al-Din and Aybak went,
and both sides encamped opposite each other.
And when it was midnight,
Aybak rose up to go and overpower the army of Erbil.
And Badr al-Din restrained him greatly, urging him to wait until morning dawned,
but he did not accept it.
Instead, he mounted and had the men of his party mount,
and Badr al-Din {OCR: ܫܲܕܪܐܲܠܕܝܼܢ} was compelled to follow him as well.
And they went and encountered Muzaffar al-Din.
